{"notes": "Visit 3 (4:00). Table: everything is dark, so it is all connected to the start. The bottom line runs to ~(27.7,16.7). The top line now runs past the old stopping point, dips near (23,7.7) and rises to ~(27.5,3.5), so the upper fork/tail exists and joins. The doubled stretch from visit 2 (x=9-10) is still there, and the top line looks doubled or overlapping from about x=9 to x=19. That is redundant and a possible misfire when pushed. There are no hand labels, so I still can't say who placed what and won't score on attribution.

Tom: I didn't hear him this visit, but Leo, Maya and Priya all treat the upper fork as his, and Leo's 'On it, Tom' suggests he spoke up and claimed it. The fork is now built and connected, which fits, but I haven't seen him place anything. Ask him directly about the fork and the bottom line. Possibly a quiet but real contributor.

Maya: Backed off and handed the fork over ('I'll stay off it'). She is acting as quality checker and promised to shout if she spots a break. Good delegation and trust, and leadership still looks strongest. Execution is unverified.

Priya: Checked connectivity from the nose, gave Tom space and offered help closing gaps. Supportive and collaborative. Still ask her privately about the overlap and the role changes.

Leo: Said he would check the doubled middle of the back, but it is still doubled. Good intent, no visible result yet. He is mostly coordinating.

Next: is the overlap resolved or harmless, and does the push run clean? Ask the team privately who built what."}
